to: PrairieLearn hiring team via the application channel in the HN post
subject: Application — Full-Stack Software Engineer — evidence-first delivery
body:
Dear PrairieLearn hiring team,

I'm writing about the Full-Stack Software Engineer role posted in the July 2026 HN Who's Hiring thread. PrairieLearn is an assessment-authoring platform used by universities to run computational homework and exams, so LLM integration in your context isn't the usual chatbot layer — it's autograding, question generation, and academic-integrity signal, all under scrutiny by faculty who will notice when a wrong answer gets marked correct or a hallucinated hint appears in a student's transcript. What I can bring to that seam concretely: bounded delivery on the acceptance-test-first shape (given input X, the LLM path produces Y and refuses on Z), with an append-only receipt of what actually ran so a suspicious grade next month has an audit trail.

Evidence aligned to the spec (LLM integration, TypeScript, React, Node.js):
- https://hfo-games.pages.dev/ — 21 live, no-login browser games (TypeScript/JS in production, short feedback loops).
- https://github.com/TTaoGaming/hfo-gen-133 — evidence-gated agent workflow, held-out checks, append-only receipts, operator-gated effects.
- The four public Suika DLC variants demonstrate reuse under a strict 'don't count staged artifacts as external results' rule.

I have intentionally not claimed years, degrees, work authorization, or location eligibility not established by the public portfolio; those need to be confirmed in the ATS form.

Book a 15-minute call if a bounded LLM-in-assessment conversation is useful: {{OPERATOR_BOOKING_LINK}}.

— TTaoGaming
https://github.com/TTaoGaming
